one_liner: Single-header C++14 port of mapbox/delaunator for 2D Delaunay; about 10% faster than JS at 1M points, roughly matches Triangle.
what_it_does: Computes the unconstrained Delaunay triangulation of a 2D point set. Input is a flat std::vector<double> (x0, y0, x1, y1, ...) passed to the delaunator::Delaunator constructor, and the result is public index arrays: triangles (three point indices per triangle), halfedges (index of the opposite half-edge, or INVALID_INDEX on the hull) and hull_prev/hull_next/hull_tri/hull_start for the convex hull. It is a port of the JavaScript mapbox/delaunator with the same array layout, not a drop-in for Triangle or CGAL APIs.
how_it_is_fast: It uses the sweep-hull incremental scheme (as in S-hull). It seeds a triangle near the bounding-box centre, sorts all points by distance from that triangle's circumcentre and inserts them in order, so each new point lies outside the current convex hull. A visible hull edge is found through a hash of hull vertices keyed by pseudo-angle (about sqrt(n) buckets). The new fan of triangles is fixed up by Lawson edge flips (legalize), using an explicit stack instead of recursion (PR #12). Everything lives in flat, pre-reserved index vectors (2n-5 triangles), so there is no per-triangle allocation or pointer-based mesh.
when_to_use: Unconstrained 2D Delaunay of well-spread double-precision points (GIS nodes, random samples, projected point clouds) up to a few million points, single-threaded
You want one small MIT-licensed header instead of pulling in CGAL or Triangle, and can patch it locally
You need the triangles/halfedges array layout of mapbox/delaunator to share code or data with the JS original
Inputs that should stay as doubles rather than being quantised to int32 as Delaunay32 requires
when_not_to_use: Degenerate or near-degenerate input (many collinear or cocircular points, snapped grids, huge coordinate ranges): predicates are plain double arithmetic, and open issues report an infinite loop in legalize() (#16, fix PR #32 unmerged), an orient robustness bug (#43) and division by zero when choosing the third seed point (#46)
Constrained edges, polygons with holes or quality meshing: not supported (issue #35); use detria, CDT or Triangle

Raw speed on large sets: in the Delaunay32 table (1M points, Apple M1) it takes 542.0 ms against 131.6 ms for single-thread Delaunay32 and 314.1 ms for single-thread Fade2D, and it has no parallel mode
Projects that need an upstream that takes fixes: no commits since 2018-10-07, 24 open issues, fix PRs #28, #30 and #32 unmerged

integration.form: source-drop (single header include/delaunator.hpp; not safe to include from more than one translation unit as shipped)
integration.dependencies: none beyond the C++ standard library; the repo's tests and benchmarks pull Catch 2.4.0, RapidJSON 1.1.0 and Google Benchmark 1.2.0 through mason
integration.min_toolchain: C++14 (CMakeLists sets CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD 14); some toolchains (MSVC, newer GCC) need #include <tuple> added because std::tie is used without it (issues #26, #39, PR #37)
integration.platforms: any (portable scalar C++ on doubles, no SIMD)
integration.thread_safety: not documented; there is no global or static mutable state, so separate Delaunator objects can be built on separate threads, but each triangulation is single-threaded
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial: same algorithm and output arrays as mapbox/delaunator (JS), but a C++ API; not a drop-in for Triangle or CGAL

gotchas: The out-of-class member definitions (constructor, legalize, add_triangle, link, get_hull_area) are not marked inline, so including delaunator.hpp from two .cpp files fails to link with duplicate symbols (issue #33, LNK2005; PR #30 'inline Delaunator methods' unmerged). Include it from one translation unit or add inline yourself.
The object stores `std::vector<double> const& coords`, a reference to your input. Passing a temporary leaves a dangling reference, and the input vector must outlive the Delaunator.

max_x/max_y start at std::numeric_limits<double>::min() (the smallest positive double, not the lowest value), so the bounding box is wrong when all x or all y coordinates are negative. This shifts the seed-point choice (issue #27; PR #28 'Use lowest instead of min' unmerged).

Collinear input throws std::runtime_error("not triangulation"), but with fewer than two distinct points the seed indices stay INVALID_INDEX and coords is read out of bounds before that check. Validate the input size and distinctness first. Near-duplicate points (within DBL_EPSILON) are silently skipped.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Delaunay32 (already catalogued) is 4.1x faster single-threaded on 1M points, uses exact integer predicates and supports constraints, so prefer it unless you need double input without int32 quantisation or a C++14-only toolchain. Pick delaunator-cpp over detria or CDT only for unconstrained point sets, where it is simpler and, per the Delaunay32 table, 1.8x faster than CDT 1.4.5.
verified_claims_summary: First-party only: a 2018-09-29 Google Benchmark run in the README (unnamed '4 X 2300 MHz' CPU, compiler unstated, CMake release flags -O3) triangulates 1M uniform random points in 994 ms. PR #8 settles on about 10% faster than the JS original at 1M points, with no hardware or Node version stated, after the author's '6 times faster' claim was challenged as JIT warmup. The only C++ comparison is the competitor-run Delaunay32 README table (1M unique integer points, Apple M1, one thread, flags not stated): 542.0 ms vs Triangle 1.6 at 584.0 ms (about 1.08x) and CDT 1.4.5 at 988.7 ms, but behind Delaunay32 (131.6 ms) and Fade2D 2.17.3 (314.1 ms).
status_note: Abandoned since 2018-10-07 (88 commits, 24 open issues including an infinite loop), but MIT-licensed and about 600 lines in one header, so it is easy to vendor and patch. The abellgithub/delaunator-cpp fork (last commit 2025-04-18) carries the lowest() fix, header-only and compiled build modes, and collinear and degenerate-case handling.
